mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship: Team A's own shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR (measuring attacking accuracy) crossed with Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST (measuring defensive on-target suppression). Both dimensions must be active simultaneously — not one observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's shot-to-on-target ratio is low (many shots, few on target) and the opponent allows a below-average rate of shots on target, the resulting shots_on_target FOR is suppressed further than either factor alone would suggest — a compounding, non-additive relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly considered alongside Team B's defensive suppression of shots on target allowed, to test whether a low-accuracy attacker facing a permissive shot-on-target defence produces a different shots_on_target total than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint product of two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR for Team A, plus shots_on_target AGAINST for Team B) — it cannot be reduced to a single observable mirrored against what the opponent allows, nor to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's recent fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is substantially elevated above its ALL_PRIOR baseline, while simultaneously Team A's yellow_cards AGAINST (ALL_PRIOR) is also elevated above competition context. Both conditions must hold together — a two-observable, regime-shift cross.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's foul rate has recently escalated into a high-foul regime AND the opponent historically draws elevated yellow cards from opponents, yellow_cards FOR (Team B) rises above what either team's standalone card or foul average would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate has diverged sharply between its all-prior average and its recent 5 matches (all-prior ~10.5 FOR, recent ~15.2 FOR), while Team A concedes fouls at a stable rate. The joint relationship between Team B's recent foul escalation and Team A's yellow-card-against rate tests whether a high-fouling visiting team facing a team that draws above-average yellow cards from opponents produces a non-linear spike in cards, beyond what either team's individual card or foul rate alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two teams, conditioned on a within-team recent-vs-prior regime shift in one observable — not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-prior comparison of the same observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on half (first vs second) simultaneously for both Team A's corner production and Team B's corner concession. The mechanism requires the within-match half split for both sides at once — not just one team's half split in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half produces a higher combined corner total than the first half, and this asymmetry is amplified when Team A's second-half corner production tendency is combined with Team B's elevated second-half corner concession tendency — the joint second-half corner rate rises above what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks show a meaningful first-half vs second-half split (1H ~1.92 FOR, 2H ~2.05 FOR all-prior), while Team B concedes corners at a higher rate in the second half than the first (1H ~2.52 AGAINST, 2H ~3.14 AGAINST all-prior). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — Team A's corner production by half crossed with Team B's corner concession by half — tests whether the second half produces a disproportionately elevated corner total relative to the first half, beyond what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split applied jointly to both teams' corner observables simultaneously — it is not a single observable with one coarse band, and it is not a simple home/away or recent/prior split. The joint half-level asymmetry across both sides is the novel structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's yellow_cards FOR (RECENT_5) is in a declining regime relative to ALL_PRIOR, while Team B's fouls FOR (RECENT_5) is in an escalating regime relative to ALL_PRIOR. The asymmetry across teams and across observables (cards vs fouls) is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team is in a low-card recent regime and the opposing team is in a high-foul recent regime, the second-half cards (cards_2h) distribution becomes asymmetric — concentrated on the high-fouling team — rather than balanced, and the total cards_2h rises above competition context baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards FOR have dropped sharply in recent matches (all-prior ~2.31, recent ~1.2) while Team B's fouls FOR have spiked (all-prior ~10.5, recent ~15.2). The asymmetric divergence between one team's disciplinary restraint trend and the other team's foul escalation trend — measured as a cross-team, cross-observable regime divergence — tests whether the cards_2h (second-half cards) total is elevated when one side is in a high-foul regime and the other is in a low-card regime, creating an asymmetric second-half card distribution.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three distinct observables (yellow_cards, fouls, cards_2h) across two teams in opposing regime directions — a cross-team, cross-observable asymmetric divergence. It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band, nor to a simple recent-vs-prior comparison of the same observable for one team.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's possession FOR being in a low-possession regime (below competition context of 50%) both all-prior and in recent matches, AND (2) Team A playing at home where their possession is highest. The joint possession-asymmetry across both teams simultaneously — not just one team's possession split — is the conditioning structure, and the outcome tested is whether shots and corners FOR (Team A) are elevated under this joint condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a home team with above-average home possession faces a visiting team with a structural low-possession profile, the home team's shots FOR and corner_kicks FOR rise above what either team's standalone possession or shot/corner averages would predict — possession asymmetry compounds attacking volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B operates with a persistent below-average possession share (all-prior ~44.8%, recent ~42.4%) while also conceding above-average possession to opponents (opponents hold ~55.2% against Team B). Team A, playing at home, holds slightly above-average possession at home (~50.8%) but below average away. The joint relationship between Team B's structural low-possession profile and Team A's home possession tendency tests whether a possession-asymmetric match (one team structurally dominant in possession) produces a different shots and corner kicks distribution than possession-balanced matches — specifically whether Team A's shots FOR and corners FOR are elevated beyond their own baseline when facing a team that structurally cedes possession.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship among three distinct observables (possession, shots, corner_kicks) conditioned on two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (Team A's home possession tendency AND Team B's structural away low-possession profile). It cannot be reduced to one observable with one band.
